Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Greenville-Spartanburg SC
655 PM EST Sat Nov 21 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Likelihood of dense fog early Monday morning has increased.

Aviation discussion was updated to reflect the 00Z TAFs.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1. Rain chances continue to increase through tonight with rainfall
possible across much of the forecast area.
2. Cooler from Tuesday onward with increasing precipitation
chances by midweek.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Key message 1: Rain chances continue to increase through tonight with 
rainfall possible across much of the forecast area. 

The first rounds of rainfall started this morning and continue to 
spread throughout the area this afternoon and evening. An area of 
low pressure off the Carolina coastline gradually strengthens as it 
moves off toward the north/northeast. Some of the outer bands of 
rain are still expected to reach numerous locations, especially east 
of the mountains through tonight and linger into Sunday morning. 
Despite the moisture increasing throughout the day, nearby soundings 
taken this morning and model soundings later on show an unsaturated 
boundary layer, with a gradual moistening into the evening hours. 
What this means is any precip falling from these first rounds is 
hitting much drier air below and mostly evaporating before reaching 
the ground. However, as this continues, the air should become more 
moist and allow for rainfall to reach the ground later in the day 
and into the overnight. So, for rainfall amounts, depending on how 
much dry air can become saturated, still not looking at a lot, but 
given the persistent dry conditions, anything is better than 
nothing. Still looking at a range of 0.10"-1", with the higher 
amount occurring wherever a heavier band can set up. Currently, this 
area looks to be NE Georgia and locations east of the mountains.
Expect rainfall to taper off Sunday morning and the system to be 
gone by Sunday night.


Key message 2: Cooler from Tuesday onward with increasing 
precipitation chances by midweek.

A cold front approaches the area Monday/Monday night, increasing 
daytime temps before spilling in cooler air. Guidance is not keen on 
the frontal passage holding together and breaks it up over the 
mountains. Meanwhile, the southern stream pushes to keep some amount 
of moisture across the majority of the CWA Monday onward. Current 
guidance does allow for cooler temps to filter in on Tuesday and 
remain through Day 7. 

Additionally, long range models are depicting a pattern change for 
the southeast as a split trough develops two different areas of low 
pressure over the central/southern CONUS and ejects the southern 
system toward the CWA by midweek. Given the wonky characteristics of 
this general pattern, there appears to be a fujiwhara effect 
occurring as these two lows lift, while also signaling a weak 
Miller B type pattern through the end of the week. What this signals 
for the southeast is an uptick in rain chances Wednesday into 
Thursday, with lingering precip chances through at least Friday. 
These systems are far out in the forecast period and a lot will 
change, but there is still an ample amount of uncertainty to how 
this systems impacts the CWA. If the system takes a more northern 
track, less impacts. If colder air is in place, the higher 
elevations could see a burst of frozen p-types. And, if the system 
strengthens and remains more southern, the area could see more 
rainfall. There is just too many uncertainties to pinpoint any 
details at this time, but we will continue to monitor.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
At KCLT and elsewhere: Thus begins our descent into lower flight
restrictions. Light precip has moved in and low clouds have
been gradually developing, but mostly VFR. Now with sunset,
and improving upslope/upglide flow, we are starting to see some
MVFR-level ceilings, mostly over Upstate SC. For the rest of
the evening, the lowest clouds will continue to develop/expand,
so all but KCLT will get a mention of at least a PROB of an MVFR
restriction until steady rain sets in and drops the cig/vis down
thru MVFR. Eventually, the guidance continues to be on board
with the ceiling dropping to IFR by daybreak. Wind will remain
NE. For Sunday, the low clouds once established will be difficult
to dislodge outside the mtns, so prevailing IFR was kept with wind
remaining N to NE. As the low shifts off to the east late Sunday,
we might get the wind to come around enough to the N to provide for
some downslope flow that will take care of the lowest cloud decks.

Outlook: Widespread fog may develop early Monday with vis
restrictions down to VLIFR possible. Increased rain chances and
possible restrictions return by midweek.
